environment_caveats: Audited the Cloudflare Pages staging preview because clients/quality-contracting-inc.json still has no apex_cutover.completed_at. HOWEVER, as of this run https://qualitycontracting.us/ is already serving the new Rank AI build (server: cloudflare, same Astro asset set, title 'Restoration Services in Central Massachusetts...', IndexNow key file /92370eb0990e4d9a832d8b93a4bd94ef.txt returns 200, no x-robots-tag). The cutover appears to have happened without being recorded in the client record.

GET https://staging.rankai-quality-contracting-inc.pages.dev/ returns x-robots-tag: noindex (Cloudflare Pages preview injection). is-crawlable fails on all 6 URLs and deflates SEO to 69. SEO is inconclusive on the staging run and was excluded from every verdict; verdicts use performance, accessibility and best_practices only.

Diagnostic only, not in audited_urls: one desktop Lighthouse run against the apex homepage https://qualitycontracting.us/ returned performance 98, accessibility 100, best_practices 100, SEO 100, LCP 1106ms, CLS 0.036. SEO 100 on the apex confirms is-crawlable is the only thing holding the staging SEO score down.

Canonical tags on all 6 staging pages point to https://qualitycontracting.us/..., so the DataForSEO canonical self-reference check reports false on all 6. Correct for a staging preview; not recorded as an issue.

Lighthouse 13.4.0 ran desktop only (for_mobile false, cpuSlowdownMultiplier 1, throughputKbps 10240). Mobile performance would typically run 10-20 points lower and the homepage CLS would very likely be worse.

URL set held identical to the 2026-08-27 baseline for regression continuity. url-plan.json now has four service-landing pages tied at priority 9.0 (fire-damage, mold-remediation, roofing, water-damage in plan order); water-damage and fire-damage were kept from the tie.
